solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Insecure Ryder Cup team employing new iron

indicators.note: a team employing someone takes them on, so the team's letters hold the new recruit inside

parts.note: the United States side in golf's Ryder Cup
N is the abbreviation for new
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A golf team feels shaky after bringing in an unfamiliar iron club.
explanation.walkthrough: U(N)SA + FE. 'Iron' looks like a golf club in the Ryder Cup picture, but it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsafe is not secure, so the two words are close synonyms describing exposure to danger.

clue.text: Reverse work of seamstress you and I endless check over

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means the whole string is read from the bottom up
without an end, the word for check loses its final letter

parts.note: you and I together are we
to snub is to rebuff or check someone

explanation.surface: A seamstress and a friend agree to look over each other's stitching.
explanation.walkthrough: WE + SNU(b), all reversed, gives UNSEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress sews; undoing her stitches is the opposite action, so to unsew is that labour undone.

clue.text: Actor sadly backs out at about fifty

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the number
something done sadly goes badly, so these letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: the letters as printed, to be rearranged
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A performer, sadly, pulls out of a show when he is around fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: Scott Bakula starred in the TV series Quantum Leap and Star Trek: Enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott Bakula is an American television and film performer, so he is one example of the category named.

clue.text: Knowing for a little while cheese is out

indicators.note: the cheese being out means it is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: for a short time
Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Someone notes that, for the moment, there is no cheese left.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIEFLY without BRIE leaves FLY. FLY meaning knowing or sharp is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a fly person is shrewd and street-wise, alert to tricks, which matches being knowing.

clue.text: Increasingly submissive timekeepers riled out of spite

indicators.note: riled means stirred up, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
out of here means taken away from, so one word's letters are removed from the other

parts.note: the word as printed
the word as printed, whose letters are removed

explanation.surface: Timekeepers who have been riled grow more docile, out of sheer spite.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S, P, I, T, E from TIMEKEEPERS leaves M, E, K, E, E, R, rearranged as MEEKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Meek means mild and submissive, and the comparative form describes someone growing more so.

clue.text: Me and my mother, embracing at least

indicators.note: the mother is embracing, so her letters wrap round the others

parts.note: mum is a British word for mother
at home means in
me, the speaker, is I
my shortened to M', as in m'lud

explanation.surface: A child describes being hugged by their mother, at the very least.
explanation.walkthrough: MUM holds IN + I + M to make M(INIM)UM.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum is the smallest possible amount, which is the least that can be given or accepted.

clue.text: Now vocal setter? Believable, as you can't prove otherwise!

definitions.text: Believable, as you can't prove otherwise!

parts.note: someone now speaking is no longer silent: an ex-silent person
Io is the pseudonym of this puzzle's compiler

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, finally speaking up, claims to be credible because nobody can disprove him.
explanation.walkthrough: Ex silentio is Latin for 'from silence'; an argument ex silentio rests on the absence of contrary evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument from silence treats a claim as plausible simply because no record contradicts it, the sense the definition describes.

clue.text: Ultimately the King and Queen are human, Pope said

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word
R for Rex, Latin for king
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Even royalty are only mortal, as the poet Alexander Pope observed.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope wrote 'To err is human, to forgive divine'; the definition borrows his line.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope's maxim equates making mistakes with being human, so to make mistakes is what the quoted words describe.

clue.text: Surging mass is enduring great heat when disembarking?

indicators.note: disembarking means getting off the ship, and S stands for ship, so that letter goes

parts.note: to swelter is to suffer in oppressive heat

explanation.surface: A crowd pours off a ship into blistering heat.
explanation.walkthrough: SWELTER loses its S, the abbreviation for ship, leaving WELTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A welter is a confused heap or a turbulent rolling mass, such as heaving waves or a jumble of things.

clue.text: Peewee having taken wife back on, I go in search of new bird

definitions.text: I go in search of new bird

indicators.note: having taken in something means holding it inside

parts.note: a titch is British slang for a very small person
W is the abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: back means the next short word is read the other way round

parts.note: on in the sense of about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone called Peewee remarries the wife he once left and sets off to find a new partner.
explanation.walkthrough: T(W)ITCH + ER. 'Peewee' looks like the lapwing, a bird, but it means a small person; 'bird' also hints at a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitcher is a British birdwatcher who travels to spot rare species for their list, chasing each new sighting.

clue.text: Flyer Spoonerised the part everyone plays in physics lab

indicators.note: named after Reverend Spooner, it means the opening sounds of two words trade places

parts.note: tutti is a musical passage played by the whole orchestra; it swaps its opening sound with the next word
CERN is the particle physics laboratory near Geneva; it takes the other word's opening sound

explanation.surface: A spoonerism turns a physics experiment everyone joins in into something airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of 'tutti CERN' and you say 'sooty tern'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sooty tern is a dark-backed tropical seabird, and any bird is something that flies.

clue.text: Set about, with skill, the beginning of sherry trifle

indicators.note: set about here means turned about, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
art is skill or craft

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone makes a sherry trifle with practised skill, starting with the sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: W + ART + S is reversed. A sherry trifle is a British layered dessert, which is what the surface pretends to be about.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw is something of negligible value, as in 'not worth a straw', which is a trifle.

clue.text: What makes I'm at a low ebb periodically an appeal for company…

indicators.note: an ebb is the tide running back, so the letters are read in the backward direction
periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A lonely person feeling down writes an advert seeking companionship.
explanation.walkthrough: WLTM is lonely-hearts shorthand for 'would like to meet'. The clue runs on into 23 across, its companion abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal advertisements use this abbreviation to ask to meet someone, so it is literally a request for a partner.

clue.text: You can't further subdivide this Encyclopaedia (Vol.1 of two)?

wordplay.note: a two-volume encyclopaedia splits the alphabet, so its first volume runs A to M

explanation.surface: A reader notes that the first of two reference volumes cannot be broken down further.
explanation.walkthrough: The spine of volume one would read A TO M.
explanation.definitionFit: The name comes from Greek atomos, meaning indivisible, the smallest unit once thought impossible to split.

clue.text: Idle rest day

definitions.meaning: first meaning: undemanding, as of ... duties or a ... week with little to do
second meaning: daylight, the hours of the sun

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a day off; it is separate meanings of one word, with 'rest' also hinting at the verb to light, to settle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both slack, undemanding activity and natural daylight, as when 'it is still light out'.

clue.text: Non-electronic kit sets date of beer trading events at home

indicators.note: with nothing electronic, the E that stands for it is dropped from the next word

parts.note: gear is equipment or kit
dates in the sense of periods or eras
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A homebrew kit, with no electronics, tells you the date your beer will be ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-electronic' reads as describing the kit in the homebrew picture, but it tells you to drop the E, which stands for electronic.
explanation.definitionFit: Garage sales are informal events where householders sell unwanted items from their own garage or driveway.

clue.text: Growth's flourishing along with old cult film

indicators.note: flourishing suggests something waved about or sprouting freely, so the letters spread into a new pattern

parts.note: the letters as printed
the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A cult film about an old plant spreading out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: Ghost World is a 2001 film from Daniel Clowes's comic, starring Thora Birch and Scarlett Johansson.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2001 teen comedy-drama gained a devoted following after a modest release, the typical path of a cult picture.

clue.text: Birds, as a whole, are frightened by the parts

indicators.note: parts here is a verb: one word is parted, split open, by another set inside it

parts.note: to fear something is to be frightened by it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Birds as a whole are scared of their own body parts.
explanation.walkthrough: FEA(THE)R. The definition plays on the proverb 'birds of a feather flock together', where the word means a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of one feather are birds of the same type, so the word names a whole class or kind of creature.

clue.text: Following question about one mobile respirator?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
an ace is a one in cards
M for mobile, as in a phone listing
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: Someone queries a portable breathing device.
explanation.walkthrough: F + ACE + M + ASK. The question mark admits a face mask is only loosely a respirator.
explanation.definitionFit: A face mask covers nose and mouth to filter air for breathing, a basic form of breathing apparatus.

clue.text: Ruler against having border crossing

indicators.note: something crossing the border sits within it, so one piece lies inside the other

parts.note: a march is a frontier region
leaning against something is leaning on it

explanation.surface: A monarch resists having people crossing his frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: M(ON)ARCH. The Welsh and Scottish Marches were historic border lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a king or queen, the sovereign who rules a state.

clue.text: In sound, helps to sail a yacht

indicators.note: in sound means we judge by how the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to crew a boat is to help sail it, and a boat is her

explanation.surface: Someone lends a hand sailing a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: The yacht is the 'her' of 'crews her', said aloud. Boats are traditionally female.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiser is a yacht or motorboat with cabins, built for leisure trips rather than racing.

clue.text: Sheep attendant madly rushing about

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: A sheep and its keeper charge around in a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: On the rampage means running riot, charging about violently and uncontrollably.

clue.text: Coward's role in poky bedroom: bedding a range of high-ups

indicators.note: bedding something puts it to bed, so it lies inside the other letters

parts.note: BR is estate-agent shorthand for bedroom, poky because so short
a ridge is a range of hills or peaks

explanation.surface: A cowardly character in a cramped bedroom seduces a string of senior officials.
explanation.walkthrough: B(RIDGE)R. Noël Coward played the crime boss Mr Bridger in The Italian Job (1969).
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward, the playwright and actor, played the imprisoned crime boss Mr Bridger in a famous 1969 heist film.

clue.text: Small and combative outlaw you shouldn't have married

parts.note: to outlaw is to ban
ta is British slang for thank you, said to a gift-giver along with 'you shouldn't have'
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Someone is told they should not have married a feisty little criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: BAN + TA + M.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantam chickens are tiny and aggressive, so the word describes a small but pugnacious person, as in bantamweight boxing.

clue.text: West End Oscar's cutting about — that's very spiteful

indicators.note: cutting in means slicing between, so this piece goes inside the others
about here means turned about, so the combined letters run backwards

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A West End theatre award winner is slashing someone with a vicious review.
explanation.walkthrough: W(O)AIM reversed gives MIAOW. 'West End' looks like London's theatreland but splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: People say 'miaow' to mock a catty, spiteful remark, mimicking a cat's cry.

clue.text: Reduced 60-sec cycles

indicators.note: cycles means the letters go round, the front moving to the back

parts.note: sixty seconds is one minute, 1 MIN, with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A cut-down one-minute cycle, as on a washing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: I MIN with its I moved to the end gives MINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini describes a small, scaled-down version of something, as in a mini skirt or mini break.

clue.text: …requirement that helps to make anything so hilarious?

indicators.note: helps to make means forms part of, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: found across the end of anything, all of so, and the start of hilarious

explanation.surface: A lonely-hearts ad's requirement: someone who finds anything funny.
explanation.walkthrough: GSOH means 'good sense of humour' in lonely-hearts ads; the clue continues 11 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal advertisers often list a good sense of humour as something a prospective partner must have.

clue.text: British service chiefs abandoned Scottish beer

indicators.note: the chiefs are the leading letters of each word, and they are dropped

parts.note: the Royal Navy, Britain's senior service

explanation.surface: Top brass of a British military service walked away from their Scottish ale.
explanation.walkthrough: THE NAVY without the first letters of each word gives HE AVY.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland heavy is a name for a dark bitter ale, roughly what the English call best bitter.

clue.text: Suffering reverse concerning matter of exceptional quality

indicators.note: suffering a reverse means undergoing a turnabout, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: re means concerning
pus is the matter in an infected wound

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from a setback discusses something of fine quality.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + PUS reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal adjective for excellent or first-rate, describing something of a very high standard.

clue.text: Highly acidic character

wordplay.note: a very acidic solution has a pH of 1

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about a strongly corrosive substance.
explanation.walkthrough: The pH scale measures acidity, with the lowest numbers the most acidic.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: Unaccompanied product of R Smythe Henderson?

parts.note: Reg Smythe drew the British comic strip Andy Capp, so his product is a Capp
Ella Henderson is a British pop singer

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a solo creation by a cartoonist called Smythe Henderson.
explanation.walkthrough: A CAPP + ELLA. Andy Capp is a long-running British newspaper cartoon about a work-shy northerner.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing a cappella means performing with voices alone, without instrumental backing.

clue.text: Stage that you might need to get ready!

definitions.text: Stage that you might need to get ready!

parts.words: Stage that you might need to get ready
parts.note: surface reading: a step in preparing for something, like getting dressed
setter's reading: ready is British slang for cash, so this is the step at a cash machine where you key in a secret number

explanation.definitionFit: Entering a personal identification number is a required stage of withdrawing money from a cash machine.

clue.text: Medium large bust extends race

indicators.note: the bust is placed inside the race to stretch it out, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the mile is a running race
DD is a large bra cup size

explanation.surface: A runner of medium build finds a large chest slows her over the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: MI(DD)LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle as an adjective means intermediate, between extremes, as medium does in middle size or middle weight.

clue.text: Troubled person who's engaged in religious profession departs an unclean abode

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: this person departs, leaving the house, so those letters are taken out of it

parts.note: a pigsty is a filthy place to live

parts.words: person who's engaged in religious profession
parts.note: pi is slang for pious, describing a person who professes religion

explanation.surface: A troubled believer leaves a squalid home.
explanation.walkthrough: AN + PIGSTY without PI.
explanation.definitionFit: Angsty describes someone full of anxiety or angst, emotionally troubled and fretful.
